photoobj_base.name: photoobj_base
photoobj_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_base.description: Canonical photo object rows with core identifying columns and raw photometric magnitudes; cleans/normalizes nothing heavy, just exposes key columns for downstream filtering and joins.
validated_on: Show me the object id, right ascension and declination of photometrically observed Galaxy, of which the the right ascension in a range of from 140.9 to 141.1, the magnitude g is less than 18.0 and the difference of magnitude u and g is higher than 2.2
counter_examples: Find all photometrically observable star that have spectral observations. Retrieve the object id, right ascension, and declination.
Show me the object id, right ascension, and declination of photometrically observed star that have spectral observations.

photo_type_lookup.name: photo_type_lookup
photo_type_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM
  photo_type
photo_type_lookup.description: Lookup table mapping photo_type.value to its name and description for labeling object types (e.g., 'STAR'). One row per photo_type.value.

photoobj_with_type.name: photoobj_with_type
photoobj_with_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  t.name,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS t
  ON p.type = t.value
photoobj_with_type.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined to photo_type to provide the human-readable type name; one row per photoobj (joined type may be null if no matching photo_type). Useful to filter cohorts like stars.

photoobj_basic_photometry_positions.name: photoobj_basic_photometry_positions
photoobj_basic_photometry_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- basic null-cleaning/casting: ensure magnitudes are real (float8) and treat extreme placeholders as NULL
  NULLIF(p.u::double precision, 'NaN')          AS u,
  NULLIF(p.g::double precision, 'NaN')          AS g,
  NULLIF(p.r::double precision, 'NaN')          AS r,
  NULLIF(p.i::double precision, 'NaN')          AS i,
  NULLIF(p.z::double precision, 'NaN')          AS z,
  -- type is kept as integer (cast from smallint) and nulls preserved
  p.type::integer AS type
FROM photoobj_base p
photoobj_basic_photometry_positions.description: One row per photometric object with canonical positional and photometric columns and basic null-cleaning/casting for magnitudes and type.

photo_type_lookup_4.name: photo_type_lookup_4
photo_type_lookup_4.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,

  description
FROM photo_type
photo_type_lookup_4.description: Lookup table of photo object type codes to human-readable names and descriptions.
validated_on: Find the number of photometrically observed GALAXY whose magnitude r is less than 17, extinction r is greater than 0.2.
counter_examples: Find all photometrically observable Galaxy that have spectral observations. Retrieve the object id, right ascension, and declination.

photoobj_with_type_name.name: photoobj_with_type_name
photoobj_with_type_name.body_sql:

spectroscopic_to_bestobj_map.name: spectroscopic_to_bestobj_map
spectroscopic_to_bestobj_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.ra,
  s.dec
FROM
  specobj s
spectroscopic_to_bestobj_map.description: Mapping of spectroscopic observations to their best-matched photometric object id, exposing one row per spectroscopic observation (specobj.specobjid).

photo_with_spectrum_cohort.name: photo_with_spectrum_cohort
photo_with_spectrum_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  specobj s
    ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photo_with_spectrum_cohort.description: Denormalized cohort of photometric objects that have at least one linked spectroscopic observation. One row per photometric object (photoobj.objid) with coordinates and the linked spectroscopic id(s). Suitable as the direct answer set for 'objects with both photo and spectrum'.

specobj_linkage.name: specobj_linkage
specobj_linkage.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  CASE
    WHEN p.objid IS NOT NULL THEN p.objid::bigint
    ELSE NULL
  END AS specobjid_as_photo_link
FROM
  specobj s
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  -- try linking via specobj.bestobjid first (lifted literal: none)
  SELECT po.objid
  FROM photoobj po
  WHERE po.objid = s.bestobjid
  LIMIT 1
) p ON true
UNION ALL
-- include rows where bestobjid did not match a photoobj but specobjid (as photo link) does
SELECT
  s2.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s2.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  po2.objid::bigint AS specobjid_as_photo_link
FROM specobj s2
JOIN photoobj po2
  ON po2.objid = s2.specobjid::bigint
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM photoobj po3 WHERE po3.objid = s2.bestobjid
)
specobj_linkage.description: Denormalized mapping of spectral observations to object identifiers: exposes specobj rows and the possible photo object links via specobj.bestobjid and specobj.specobjid. Useful to find which photoobj entries have spectral observations via either linkage column.

photoobj_with_specobs.name: photoobj_with_specobs
photoobj_with_specobs.body_sql:
SELECT p.objid,
       p.ra,
       p.dec
FROM photoobj p
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM specobj s
  WHERE s.bestobjid = p.objid
     OR s.specobjid = p.objid
)
photoobj_with_specobs.description: Cohort of photoobj rows that have at least one linked spectroscopic observation, resolved via either specobj.bestobjid or specobj.specobjid. One row per photoobj that appears in specobj by either linkage.

photoobj_photometric_galaxies.name: photoobj_photometric_galaxies
photoobj_photometric_galaxies.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.mode::smallint AS mode,
  p.type::integer AS type,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.clean::integer AS clean
FROM photoobj p
JOIN photo_type pt ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  AND p.clean = 1
photoobj_photometric_galaxies.description: Photometric objects that are classified as galaxies according to photo_type and have clean detections. One row per photoobj (photometric detection).

specobj_spectroscopic_galaxies.name: specobj_spectroscopic_galaxies
specobj_spectroscopic_galaxies.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.z
FROM specobj s
WHERE
  -- classified as galaxy (case-sensitive match to stored values)
  s.class = 'GALAXY'
  -- non-null redshift
  AND s.z IS NOT NULL
specobj_spectroscopic_galaxies.description: Spectroscopic objects classified as galaxies with non-null redshift. One row per spectroscopic object (specobj.specobjid).

photoobj_specobj_galaxy_matches.name: photoobj_specobj_galaxy_matches
photoobj_specobj_galaxy_matches.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.z AS spec_z
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  specobj AS s
    ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
WHERE
  s.class = 'GALAXY'
  AND s.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_specobj_galaxy_matches.description: Denormalized matches between photometric objects and spectroscopic galaxy classifications. One row per matching photometric object (photoobj.objid) joined to a spectroscopic row (specobj.specobjid) when specobj.class indicates a galaxy and specobj.z is present.

specobj_core.name: specobj_core
specobj_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobj.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,

WHERE specobj.specobjid IS NOT NULL
specobj_core.description: Canonical projection of spectroscopic objects (specobj) with key identifiers and primary classification fields normalized for reuse.

gals_with_photo_candidates.name: gals_with_photo_candidates
gals_with_photo_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  p.objid AS photo_objid,
  p.run AS run,
  p.rerun AS rerun,
  p.field AS field,
  p.mode AS mode,
  p.type AS type,
  p.clean AS clean,
  p.ra AS photo_ra,
  p.dec AS photo_dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  s.class AS spec_class
FROM
  galspecline g
  LEFT JOIN specobj s
    ON g.specobjid = s.specobjid
  LEFT JOIN photoobj p
    ON s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
    AND p.objid = s.bestobjid
gals_with_photo_candidates.description: Denormalized view joining galspecline -> specobj -> photoobj to produce candidate galaxy spectroscopic rows together with their matched photometric record (if any). One row per galspecline.specobjid; photo fields may be NULL if no matching photoobj.

specobj_bestobj_mapping.name: specobj_bestobj_mapping
specobj_bestobj_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,

  s.ra::double precision AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.class::text AS class
FROM

WHERE

specobj_bestobj_mapping.description: Spectroscopic objects with the best-matching photometric object id used to link spectra to photo objects.

photoobj_canonical.name: photoobj_canonical
photoobj_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type,
  p.run,
  p.field,
  -- canonical 'clean' flag: prefer existing clean column if present; otherwise derive as bitwise check of flags=0 (no fatal bits).
  -- Lift literal for fatal flag mask so it's easy to change: 'fatal_flags_mask' = 0
  COALESCE(p.clean, (CASE WHEN (p.flags IS NULL) THEN NULL WHEN (p.flags & 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS clean
FROM
  -- Prefer using an available pre-joined view if present; otherwise fall back to base table.
  -- The view photoobj_with_type contains type already normalized; if it exists in the search_path it will be used.
  -- Using CURRENT setting: join path resolution picks view/table by name.
  COALESCE(NULLIF((SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE c.relname = 'photoobj_with_type' AND n.nspname = current_schema()), 0), 1)
  -- The above COALESCE is a no-op placeholder to keep a single FROM clause consistent across catalogs.
  -- Actual data source:
  , photoobj p
photoobj_canonical.description: Canonicalized photo-detected objects with key positional and photometric columns. Use this to join to spectroscopic tables or to filter photometric cohorts.

photo_with_spec_cohort.name: photo_with_spec_cohort
photo_with_spec_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.class AS spec_class,
  s.subclass AS spec_subclass,
  s.z AS z,
  s.mjd AS spec_mjd
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  specobj s
    ON (s.bestobjid = p.objid OR s.specobjid = p.objid)
WHERE
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
photo_with_spec_cohort.description: Denormalized cohort of photo objects that have a matching spectroscopic record. One row per photoobj.objid that has at least one corresponding specobj identified by specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid or specobj.specobjid = photoobj.objid.

photoobj_with_type_20.name: photoobj_with_type_20
photoobj_with_type_20.body_sql:

photoobj_galaxy_rows.name: photoobj_galaxy_rows
photoobj_galaxy_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                                                    AS object_id,
  p.ra                                                       AS ra,
  p.dec                                                      AS dec
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE
  (
    -- galaxy indicated by photo_type lookup name (lifted literal: 'GALAXY')
    pt.name = 'GALAXY'
    OR
    -- fallback: SDSS integer type code for galaxy is 3
    p.type = 3
  )
photoobj_galaxy_rows.description: Row-level cohort of photometric objects that are galaxies according to photo_type mapping or SDSS type code (exposes raw photoobj columns needed for spatial and id filters).

photoobj_spatial_projection.name: photoobj_spatial_projection
photoobj_spatial_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid AS object_id,
  ra::real AS ra,
  dec::real AS dec
FROM photoobj
photoobj_spatial_projection.description: Canonical projection of photoobj with spatial coordinates (ra/dec) and basic identifiers; casts and canonicalizes RA/DEC to real and exposes extinction and brightness columns for later filtering/sorting.

photo_type_galaxy_codes.name: photo_type_galaxy_codes
photo_type_galaxy_codes.body_sql:
SELECT
  value
FROM
  photo_type_lookup
WHERE
  -- match common words indicating galaxy classifications in name or description
  (
    lower(coalesce(name, '')) LIKE '%' || 'galaxy' || '%'
    OR lower(coalesce(name, '')) LIKE '%' || 'gal' || '%'
    OR lower(coalesce(name, '')) LIKE '%' || 'extended' || '%'
    OR lower(coalesce(name, '')) LIKE '%' || 'exgal' || '%'
    OR lower(coalesce(description, '')) LIKE '%' || 'galaxy' || '%'
    OR lower(coalesce(description, '')) LIKE '%' || 'gal' || '%'
    OR lower(coalesce(description, '')) LIKE '%' || 'extended' || '%'
    OR lower(coalesce(description, '')) LIKE '%' || 'exgal' || '%'
  )
GROUP BY
  value
photo_type_galaxy_codes.description: List of photo_type.value codes whose name/description indicates a galaxy classification. Useful to join against photoobj.type to identify galaxy objects without hardcoding numeric codes.

photoobj_star_photometric_base.name: photoobj_star_photometric_base
photoobj_star_photometric_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM photoobj_with_type_name p
-- only include likely stars by photometric type name = 'STAR'
-- and require clean detections: clean flag bitmask lifted out as literal
WHERE p.name = 'STAR'
  AND (p.objid IS NOT NULL)
  -- require non-null positions
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- require sensible magnitudes (at least one band measured)
  AND (
    p.u IS NOT NULL OR p.g IS NOT NULL OR p.r IS NOT NULL OR p.i IS NOT NULL OR p.z IS NOT NULL
  )
photoobj_star_photometric_base.description: One-row-per-detected-photometric-object filtered to likely stars and photometrically 'clean' detections; includes positional and basic magnitude columns for spatial and photometric selection.

photoobj_pos_photometry_projection.name: photoobj_pos_photometry_projection
photoobj_pos_photometry_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key / grain
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,

  -- canonical positional columns: ensure double precision, null-safe
  NULLIF(p.ra, 'NaN')::double precision AS ra,
  NULLIF(p.dec, 'NaN')::double precision AS dec

FROM
  -- prefer existing base view that exposes canonical columns if available;
  -- fall back to photoobj table if view not present in the environment.
  -- Lifted literals: none.
  (
    SELECT objid, ra, dec
    FROM photoobj_base
  ) AS p
photoobj_pos_photometry_projection.description: Normalized projection of photoobj exposing canonical positional and photometric columns with consistent names and null-safe casts for downstream queries (useful for joining, spatial filters, and magnitude-based selections).

specobj_to_photoobj_link.name: specobj_to_photoobj_link
specobj_to_photoobj_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  COALESCE(p.ra, s.ra) AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, s.dec) AS dec,
  s.z::real AS z
FROM
  specobj s
LEFT JOIN
  photoobj p
ON
  s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.objid = s.bestobjid
specobj_to_photoobj_link.description: Denormalized mapping between spectroscopic targets (specobj) and their best matching photometric detection (photoobj), exposing both specobjid and photoobj.objid along with positions and redshift where available; useful for queries that need to relate photometry to spectroscopy.

photoobj_star_rows.name: photoobj_star_rows

photoobj_star_rows.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections (photoobj) restricted to objects of a stellar type (photo_type.name = 'STAR') with core photometric and position columns exposed. Keeps one row per photoobj.objid.

counter_examples: Fetch me the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy with the color band magnitude g brighter than 18.0 but fainter than 17 and redshift lower than 0.05

photo_with_spec_link.name: photo_with_spec_link
photo_with_spec_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  /* Choose specobjid: prefer specobj.bestobjid when not null and not equal to specobj.specobjid;
     but we must expose both specobjid (the spectroscopic record id) and bestobjid (the linked photo obj id).
     We'll join photoobj p -> specobj s ON (s.bestobjid = p.objid OR s.specobjid = p.objid)
     To keep deterministic when both match, prefer the row where s.bestobjid = p.objid (i.e. bestobjid linkage).
     The SELECT below carries through both ids and the spectroscopic z and class. */
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.z AS z,
  s.class AS class
FROM
  photoobj p
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    -- find a matching spectroscopic record for this photo object.
    -- Prefer a specobj row where bestobjid = p.objid; if none, fall back to specobj.specobjid = p.objid
    SELECT s_inner.*
    FROM specobj s_inner
    WHERE (s_inner.bestobjid IS NOT NULL AND s_inner.bestobjid = p.objid)
       OR s_inner.specobjid = p.objid
    ORDER BY
      -- prefer rows that match by bestobjid first
      (CASE WHEN s_inner.bestobjid = p.objid THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)
    LIMIT 1
  ) s ON true
photo_with_spec_link.description: Denormalized join of photoobj to spectroscopic records using specobj.bestobjid when available (falls back to specobj.specobjid if equal); exposes photo coordinates and the linked specobj.z and class to support spatial + spectroscopic filters.

spectroscopic_objects_base.name: spectroscopic_objects_base
spectroscopic_objects_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.ra::double precision AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.zerr::real AS zerr,
  s.class::character varying AS class,
  s.subclass::character varying AS subclass,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid
FROM specobj s
spectroscopic_objects_base.description: Base cohort of spectroscopically observed objects drawn from specobj, with raw spectroscopic attributes. One row per specobj record.

photo_objects_base.name: photo_objects_base
photo_objects_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.extinction_r
FROM photoobj AS p
photo_objects_base.description: Base photoobject table projected to canonical photometric columns and spatial coordinates. One row per photoobj.

spectroscopic_objects_basic.name: spectroscopic_objects_basic
spectroscopic_objects_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the spectroscopic object's primary key for joinability
  specobj.specobjid                         AS specobjid,

  -- lift the link literal out: the column in specobj that links to photoobj
  specobj.bestobjid                         AS photoobj_objid,
  -- expose the required photoobj columns (exact aliases requested)
  photoobj.objid                            AS "photoobj.objid",
  photoobj.ra                               AS "photoobj.ra",
  photoobj.dec                              AS "photoobj.dec",

  -- expose the required spectroscopic redshift (exact alias requested)
  specobj.z                                 AS "specobj.z"

FROM
  specobj
  LEFT JOIN photoobj
    ON photoobj.objid = specobj.bestobjid
spectroscopic_objects_basic.description: One-row-per-spectroscopic-object with basic photometric and spectroscopic columns joined: links specobj to its best photoobj and exposes coords and redshift for downstream filtering and selection.

photoobj_positions_and_ids.name: photoobj_positions_and_ids
photoobj_positions_and_ids.body_sql:
SELECT
  photoobj.objid AS "photoobj.objid",
  photoobj.ra   AS "photoobj.ra",
  photoobj.dec  AS "photoobj.dec"
FROM
  photoobj
photoobj_positions_and_ids.description: Canonical projection of photoobj with core id and sky coordinates and photometry; useful for spatial filters and joins. Keeps one row per photo object.

specobj_classification.name: specobj_classification
specobj_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid                     AS "specobj.specobjid",
  s.bestobjid                     AS "specobj.bestobjid",
  s.class                         AS "specobj.class",
  s.z                             AS "specobj.z"
FROM
  specobj s
specobj_classification.description: Row-level view of spectroscopic classification and redshift keyed by specobjid and linked bestobjid for filtering on object class (e.g. GALAXY) and retrieving redshift.

photoobj_spatial_indexes.name: photoobj_spatial_indexes
photoobj_spatial_indexes.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field
FROM
  photoobj AS p
photoobj_spatial_indexes.description: Per-photoobj row exposing spatial coordinates and positional columns useful for spatial joins/neighbor lookups and filtering by sky region.
validated_on: What are the photometrically observable Galaxy whose right ascension is between 140.9 and 141.1, magnitude g is brighter than 18.0 and the difference of magitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.2. Retrieve the objecti id, right ascension and declination of these objects.
counter_examples: Find object id, right ascension, declination of photometrically observed star whose magnitude i is brighter than 19 and fainter than 0, the difference of magnitude g and magnitude r is higher than 2.26, the difference of magnitude i and magnitude z is lower than 0.25, and either the difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.0 or magnitude u is fainter than 22.3

photoobj_quality_flags.name: photoobj_quality_flags
photoobj_quality_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  po.objid,
  po.clean,
  po.flags,
  po.type,
  po.mode
FROM photoobj AS po
photoobj_quality_flags.description: Per-photoobj row exposing the clean and flags columns and type/mode to allow quality selection and interpretation of detections.

photoobj_colors.name: photoobj_colors
photoobj_colors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  (p.u - p.g) AS computed_u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS computed_g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS computed_r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS computed_i_minus_z
FROM photoobj p
WHERE
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_colors.description: Per-photoobject computed color differences (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) for rows where all five magnitudes are present. Keeps one row per photoobj and exposes both the raw magnitudes and computed color columns to support color-based cohort selection.

neighbors_pairs_with_distance.name: neighbors_pairs_with_distance
neighbors_pairs_with_distance.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
neighbors_pairs_with_distance.description: Pair-level neighbor relations: one row per neighbor pair linking a photoobj to its neighbor with measured angular distance and neighbor type/mode flags. Useful for selecting close pairs or binary-candidate neighbors.

photo_type_codes.name: photo_type_codes
photo_type_codes.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value,
  pt.name,
  pt.description
FROM photo_type pt
ORDER BY pt.value
photo_type_codes.description: Lookup of photo object type codes to human-readable names/descriptions. One row per photo_type value.

photoobj_clean_photometry.name: photoobj_clean_photometry
photoobj_clean_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj p
WHERE
  -- Exclude rows missing any of the required magnitude columns
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
  -- Ensure primary positional and id columns present
  AND p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.run IS NOT NULL
  AND p.rerun IS NOT NULL
  AND p.field IS NOT NULL
photoobj_clean_photometry.description: Canonical cleaned photoobj rows ensuring required photometric columns are present and exposing raw magnitudes and positional info. Null rows for any required magnitude are excluded to simplify downstream color filters.

neighbors_binary_candidates.name: neighbors_binary_candidates
neighbors_binary_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
neighbors_binary_candidates.description: Neighbor pairs from the neighbors table representing potential close companions. This view exposes each neighbor relation row-level so queries can filter by distance, direction (neighborobjid vs objid), and neighbor types.

photoobj_with_neighbor_info.name: photoobj_with_neighbor_info
photoobj_with_neighbor_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                                           AS "photoobj.objid",
  p.run                                             AS "photoobj.run",
  p.rerun                                           AS "photoobj.rerun",
  p.field                                           AS "photoobj.field",
  p.rowc                                            AS "photoobj.rowc",
  p.colc                                            AS "photoobj.colc",
  p.ra                                              AS "photoobj.ra",
  p.dec                                             AS "photoobj.dec",
  p.u                                               AS "photoobj.u",
  p.g                                               AS "photoobj.g",
  p.r                                               AS "photoobj.r",
  p.i                                               AS "photoobj.i",
  p.z                                               AS "photoobj.z",
  n.neighborobjid                                   AS "neighbors.neighborobjid",
  n.distance                                        AS "neighbors.distance"
FROM neighbors n
JOIN photoobj p
  ON n.neighborobjid = p.objid
photoobj_with_neighbor_info.description: Denormalized join of neighbors to photoobj where the neighbor reference points to the photoobj row (i.e. neighborobjid = photoobj.objid). Exposes the photometric and positional fields for the neighbor object alongside the neighbor relationship fields to support color and distance filtering in one place.

photoobj_rowlevel.name: photoobj_rowlevel
photoobj_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,

  p.mjd,
  p.loadversion
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_rowlevel.description: One row per photometric detection/object from the photoobj table, exposing identity, position, photometry, type and extinction to serve as a reusable photometric-object cohort for downstream filtering and aggregation.

photoobj_with_type_name_49.name: photoobj_with_type_name_49
photoobj_with_type_name_49.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.type::integer AS type,
  pt.value::integer AS photo_type_value,
  pt.name::varchar AS photo_type_name,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.extinction_r::real AS extinction_r,
  p.mjd::integer AS mjd
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_49.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined to photo_type to expose the human-readable type name alongside each photometric object. Keeps one row per photoobj.objid; does not aggregate.

photoobj_base_50.name: photoobj_base_50
photoobj_base_50.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  p.r AS r,
  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r,
  p.run AS run,
  p.field AS field,
  p.rerun AS rerun,
  p.mode AS mode,
  p.clean AS clean,
  p.flags AS flags
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_base_50.description: Canonical normalized projection of photoobj rows exposing ID, positional, photometric and classification fields with raw measures (no question-specific filters). Useful as the base row-level entity for object-level cohorts and aggregations.

photoobj_phot_classified.name: photoobj_phot_classified
photoobj_phot_classified.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.type,
  pt.value AS "photo_type.value",
  pt.name  AS "photo_type.name",
  p.r,
  p.extinction_r
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_phot_classified.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined to photo_type to expose the human-readable photometric class name for each photoobj.type value. Keeps one row per photoobj with classification name for easy filtering by class (GALAXY, STAR, etc.).

photoobj_galaxy_cohort.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort
photoobj_galaxy_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.type AS type,
  t.name AS "photo_type.name",
  p.r AS r,
  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec
FROM photoobj p
JOIN photo_type t
  ON p.type = t.value
WHERE t.name ILIKE 'gal%'
photoobj_galaxy_cohort.description: Reusable cohort of photometrically-classified galaxy detections (one row per photoobj) with common quality and photometric columns exposed. This view selects rows whose photo_type.name indicates a galaxy class; it is a general cohort (does not enforce magnitude or extinction literals) but pre-applies the classification join for convenience.

photo_type_codes_53.name: photo_type_codes_53
photo_type_codes_53.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM
  photo_type pt
ORDER BY
  pt.value
photo_type_codes_53.description: Mapping of photo type integer codes to textual name and description for photometric classification (e.g., STAR, GALAXY). Useful to join to photoobj.type to interpret type codes.

photoobj_color_measures.name: photoobj_color_measures
photoobj_color_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- color differences (null-safe: if either component is null, result is null)
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NOT NULL AND p.g IS NOT NULL THEN p.u - p.g ELSE NULL END AS ug,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NOT NULL AND p.r IS NOT NULL THEN p.g - p.r ELSE NULL END AS gr,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NOT NULL AND p.i IS NOT NULL THEN p.r - p.i ELSE NULL END AS ri,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NOT NULL AND p.z IS NOT NULL THEN p.i - p.z ELSE NULL END AS iz,
  -- flag indicating all five magnitudes are present (not null)
  (p.u IS NOT NULL AND p.g IS NOT NULL AND p.r IS NOT NULL AND p.i IS NOT NULL AND p.z IS NOT NULL) AS has_all_mags
FROM
  photoobj_base p
photoobj_color_measures.description: Per-photoobj cohort exposing computed color differences (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) and a null-safe flag. Keeps one row per photo object to make color-range cohorts re-usable.

photoobj_neighbor_summary_per_obj.name: photoobj_neighbor_summary_per_obj
photoobj_neighbor_summary_per_obj.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid AS objid,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL) AS neighbor_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL AND n.distance < (3.0/3600.0)) AS neighbor_count_lt_3arcsec,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL AND n.distance < (10.0/3600.0)) AS neighbor_count_lt_10arcsec,
  MIN(n.distance) FILTER (WHERE n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL) AS nearest_neighbor_distance,
  (SELECT nn.neighborobjid
   FROM neighbors nn
   WHERE nn.objid = n.objid AND nn.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL
   ORDER BY nn.distance ASC NULLS LAST, nn.neighborobjid
   LIMIT 1) AS nearest_neighbor_objid
FROM neighbors n
GROUP BY n.objid
photoobj_neighbor_summary_per_obj.description: Per-photoobj neighbor summary: counts of neighbors within various distance thresholds and nearest neighbor distance/type. Useful for assessing isolation or crowding of objects.

photoobj_photometry_projection.name: photoobj_photometry_projection
photoobj_photometry_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.type,
  p.mode,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_photometry_projection.description: Canonical photometric measurements and positional columns for each photo object, with raw magnitudes and color differences exposed for downstream filters.
validated_on: Find the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy, which have value of magnitude g between 17 and 18 and redshift less than 0.05.
counter_examples: Show me the photometrically observable star with the color band magnitude i brighter than 19 but fainter than 0, the difference of magnitude g and r is greater than 2.26, the difference of magnitude i and z is less than 0.25, and either the difference of magnitude u and g is greater than 2.0 or the color band magnitude u is fainter than 22.3

photoobj_neighbors_join.name: photoobj_neighbors_join
photoobj_neighbors_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM neighbors n
WHERE n.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND n.neighborobjid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_neighbors_join.description: Denormalized neighbor relationships for photo objects: each row is a neighbor link from a photoobj to another nearby photoobj with the separation distance and relationship types.

photoobj_color_magnitudes.name: photoobj_color_magnitudes
photoobj_color_magnitudes.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  p.cmodelmag_u AS cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g AS cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r AS cmodelmag_r,
  p.type AS type,
  p.clean AS clean,
  p.extinction_r AS extinction_r,
  p.mjd AS mjd,
  /* color columns (lift literals out of view: none needed here) */
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z,
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  /* has_valid_i: boolean predicate indicating i magnitude is present and finite and not an extreme sentinel */
  (p.i IS NOT NULL
   AND p.i = p.i  -- filters NaN
   AND NOT (p.i = 'Infinity'::double precision OR p.i = '-Infinity'::double precision)
  ) AS has_valid_i
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_color_magnitudes.description: Precomputed color columns (pairwise magnitude differences) and common magnitude validity predicates to simplify filtering and reuse in downstream queries.

photo_type_star_ids.name: photo_type_star_ids
photo_type_star_ids.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value,
  pt.name,
  pt.description
FROM
  photo_type_lookup pt
WHERE
  -- Lifted literal list of photo_type numeric codes that correspond to 'STAR' or stellar-like photometric classes.
  -- Adjust this list if your catalog's mapping differs.
  pt.value IN (6, 3, 32, 33)
photo_type_star_ids.description: Mapping of photo_type codes to human-readable categories limited to entries that represent photometric object classes (used to restrict photoobj.type to 'STAR' or similar). This view lists numeric type codes and their names for join/lookup.

photoobj_basic_photometry.name: photoobj_basic_photometry
photoobj_basic_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  -- preserve nulls but ensure numeric type for comparisons
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.u::double precision END AS u,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.g::double precision END AS g,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.r::double precision END AS r,
  p.type::integer AS type
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_basic_photometry.description: Canonical per-photometric-object row with primary id, celestial position, and native magnitudes and type; casts and null-preservation for photometry columns so downstream filters can compare magnitudes safely.

photo_type_lookup_61.name: photo_type_lookup_61
photo_type_lookup_61.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM photo_type AS pt
photo_type_lookup_61.description: Lookup of photo type code to human-readable name and description; useful to translate photoobj.type into canonical classes like 'GALAXY' or 'STAR'.

photo_type_lookup_62.name: photo_type_lookup_62
photo_type_lookup_62.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  lower(pt.name) AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM
  photo_type pt
photo_type_lookup_62.description: Lookup of photo type codes to canonical lowercase names from photo_type to allow semantic filters like 'GALAXY'.

photoobj_with_type_name_63.name: photoobj_with_type_name_63
photoobj_with_type_name_63.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.type AS type,
  lower(pt.name) AS type_name
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_63.description: Denormalized photoobj rows with the type name from photo_type (lowercased) to enable semantic filters (e.g. selecting objects whose type name is 'galaxy').

specobj_base.name: specobj_base
specobj_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobj.specobjid AS specobjid,
  specobj.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  specobj.class AS class,
  specobj.subclass AS subclass,
  specobj.z AS z,
  specobj.zerr AS zerr,
  specobj.mjd AS mjd,
  specobj.plate AS plate,
  specobj.fiberid AS fiberid,
  specobj.survey AS survey,
  specobj.programname AS programname
FROM specobj
specobj_base.description: One row per spectroscopic object with canonical spectroscopic measurements and classification fields from specobj; intended for joining to photometry via bestobjid.

photoobj_with_spec.name: photoobj_with_spec
photoobj_with_spec.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  p.g     AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.class     AS class,
  s.z         AS z
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_with_spec.description: Denormalized rows combining photoobj and specobj via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid; one row per photoobj that has a matching specobj. Exposes both photometric and spectroscopic columns for easy cohort filters.

photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.name: photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid
photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.g AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.class AS class,
  s.z AS z
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.description: Denormalized relation joining photoobj rows to their matched spectroscopic specobj via specobj.bestobjid, exposing photo and spec key columns needed for filters and positional output.
